posts.text:
We've finally made it to November... holy crap October was brutal. 

Per Morgan Stanley data, the recent hedge fund de-grossing was the highest in the past 10 years. 

Exceeding the:  
- 2016 Chinese stock market crash
- 2018 Volmageddon
- March 2020 COVID crash
- 2021 Archegos collapse / Evergrande crisis
- 2022 bear market

Goldman's prime brokerage desk reported on the 26th that it had also seen ~$20B of selling over 2 weeks vs. $23 billion during July's entire unwind. 

From $HOOD short interest data, from Sept -> Oct short float also increased from:

$AAOI: 12.5% -> 19.84%+ 
$AEVA: 11% -> 25.64%+ 
$CBRS: 12.25% -> 20.12%+
$AEHR: 14.33% -> 17.93%+
$TSEM: 2.15% -> 4.73%+
$CIFR: 19.94% -> 25.39%+
$LWLG: 15.24% ->19.12%+ 
$OKLO: 17.72% ->22.93%+
$CRWV: 17.91% ->26.58%+

Substantial deleveraging coinciding with surging short interest, kinda looks like a July setup after Midterms? 

The recent rotation also kinda pushed names like $CRWD and cybersecurity to bubble valuations into hundreds of fwd P/E... 

Earnings on many AI capex + bottlenecks (not all like $INTC) looked strong: 

eg. $AXTI guided annualized Q4 = 23.7x P/E now, not including potential InP substrate hikes + capacity expansion that can compress it to single digits.

- No signs of $MSFT / $AMZN materially cutting capex, while $SPCX secures $40B more for GPU procurement. 

Slightly painful, but I think the AI capex trade (specifically photonics/memory) is a generational opportunity, with extreme volatility in between.

posts.name: jeroen blokland
posts.text:
De Raad van State is bijzonder kritisch over de nieuwe box 3-plannen.

Het advies is duidelijk: trek het huidige wetsvoorstel in en kom met een nieuw stelsel dat in 2030 ingaat.

En daarmee worden meteen een paar problemen opgelost!

Het was namelijk al de bedoeling om vanaf 2030 ook goud en bitcoin onder de vermogenswinstbelasting te brengen. 

Als het kabinet het advies van de Raad van State volgt en in 2030 in één keer overstapt op een nieuw stelsel, verdwijnt ook het probleem van de tijdelijke ongelijke behandeling tussen vermogensaanwas- en vermogenswinstbelasting.

Daarmee verdwijnt bovendien een belangrijke aanleiding voor nieuwe rechtszaken.
En dan zijn ook die 252 extra fte die de Belastingdienst tijdelijk nodig zou hebben voor de voorgestelde wijzigingen niet meer nodig. 

Mooi, want het kabinet heeft voor de zoveelste keer beloofd de overheid nu écht kleiner te maken. Overigens waren er voor de nieuwe box 3-plannen al 900 extra fte voorzien.

Dus we moeten niet te snel conclusies trekken. En al helemaal niet stoppen met beleggen vanwege de onzekerheid rond box 3.

Dat neemt niet weg dat een aantal fundamentele problemen gewoon blijft bestaan. Zoals het exorbitant hoge belastingtarief van 36% en het feit dat inflatie niet wordt gecompenseerd. Je betaalt dus ook belasting over rendement dat je koopkracht helemaal niet vergroot.  Daar schreef ik eerder al een artikel over.

De Raad van State heeft bovendien een belangrijk punt: waarom met zoveel haast een ingewikkeld belastingstelsel invoeren als zelfs de Belastingdienst aangeeft dat het niet uitvoerbaar is?

Terug naar de tekentafel is dan ook een goed idee. We schreven op onze Substack al twee keer uitgebreid over box 3 en de gevolgen voor beleggers.

The global copper market is extremely tight:

China's copper import premium over London Metal Exchange (LME) prices has surpassed $200 per ton, the largest premium on record.

The Yangshan premium, named after a Shanghai port that serves as a major hub for Chinese copper imports, has more than doubled over the last 3 months.

Since the beginning of 2026, this figure has surged +700%.

Furthermore, the premium of spot prices over three-month futures on the LME widened to $217 per ton, the largest since mid-August.

This has been driven by strong Chinese copper demand and domestic inventories falling below typical seasonal levels.

At the same time, expectations of potential US tariffs on refined copper have redirected hundreds of thousands of tons of copper to the US, leaving global inventories heavily concentrated in the country.

The physical copper supply squeeze is far from over.

By comparison, at the height of the 2000 Dot-Com Bubble, this metric grew +6.2%.

Since Q4 2022, private fixed investment in information processing equipment and software has surged +61%, or +$671 billion.

As a % of GDP, this metric is up to a record 5.4%, significantly surpassing the previous high of 4.5% recorded in Q4 2000.

The scale of US AI investment is unlike anything seen before.

BREAKING: The US goods trade deficit widened by -$2.8 billion in September, or -2.1%, to -$134.9 billion, its widest gap since March 2025.

Imports rose +$8.1 billion, or +2.4%, to a record $344.2 billion.

This jump was led by a +7.5% MoM increase in capital goods, which include computers and accessories, semiconductors, and telecommunications equipment fueling the AI buildout.

Now, the capital goods deficit has widened by -$54.3 billion YoY, accounting for more than the entire increase in the overall trade deficit.

The US trade deficit is rapidly widening again.

posts.text:
Multiple roommates.  Ramen noodles.  Near public transportation.  Respect to the people who do whatever it takes.  

I worked as a bartender.  Bar-back. $2.15 an hr plus whatever tips got shared.  Worked at a retail store. Never had benefits at any job.  

Had 5 roommates in a 3 br apt.  Ate lousy food out of cans and ate  a ton of peanuts and shit food  at happy hour.  Had credit cards ripped up.  Etc.  

But I learned a ton.  Taught me what was right and wrong about running a business by watching my bosses and their bosses 

Yeah I know. It was much easier then, when inflation was 15 pct and national unemployment was 10 %.  I know I was fortunate when I finally got fired from the store, and had to start my own business with zero cash.   Bill collectors everywhere. 
Even luckier when I found my first customer so I could pay my bills

But I recognize it’s so much harder today.  

Which is why I respect the people who are willing to do what it takes to get started
